input.claim_text: On 8 February 2024 my son was kicking a soccer ball in the backyard and it smashed straight through our sliding glass door. The whole pane shattered and we've had to board it up until it can be replaced. I think it'll cost around $650 to fix. (Policyholder with RAA home insurance.)

output.cause: soccer ball kicked into sliding glass door

input.query: Accidental breakage of glass sliding door coverage

output.answer:
Based on the provided excerpts, the **Accidental Breakage of Glass and Sanitary Fixtures** Additional Benefit states that, if **Home** is shown on your Certificate of Insurance, RAA will cover the cost of repairing or replacing "any part of any: fixed glass forming part of the Insured Property including windows" if accidentally broken [RAA Contents PDS, page 52].

A glass sliding door, being a fixed glass component of the home, would generally fall under this description of "fixed glass forming part of the Insured Property" — however, the excerpts do not explicitly name "sliding doors" as an example (only "windows" is specifically mentioned) [RAA Contents PDS, page 52].

Note the following exclusions apply to this benefit, none of which specifically reference sliding doors, but are worth noting:
- Repairing scratches where the break does not extend through the entire thickness of the item
- Glass in a glasshouse or greenhouse
- Repair or replacement of tiles, tiled fixtures, or splashbacks (tiled or glass)
- Toilet seats
- Glass forming part of a stove, heater, oven, or cooktop damaged by direct heat
- Picture tubes/screens of televisions or visual display units
- Glass in radios, clocks, vases, ornaments, lamps, or photo frames
[RAA Contents PDS, page 52]

This benefit is also subject to the General Exclusions and other policy terms and conditions, and the applicable limit is the **Sum Insured** [RAA Contents PDS, page 35].
